name: Pakistan
fact: At Taxila, ancient city ruins and monasteries tell the story of an early Buddhist learning centre.

name: Palau
fact: The Rock Islands include limestone islands shaped like mushrooms above turquoise lagoons.

name: Palestine
fact: Bethlehem's Church of the Nativity preserves floor mosaics from an earlier fourth-century church.

name: Panama
fact: Darién National Park forms a natural bridge between North and South America, with rainforest and mangroves.

name: Papua New Guinea
fact: At Kuk, ancient farmers drained wetlands by digging ditches with wooden tools.

name: Paraguay
fact: The ruins at Trinidad de Paraná preserve a Jesuit mission settlement with churches and a central square.

name: Peru
fact: The Inca settlement Machu Picchu stands high in the Andes, among forested mountain slopes.

name: Philippines
fact: Ifugao farmers shaped mountain slopes into stepped rice fields that follow the land's curves.

name: Poland
fact: Wieliczka and Bochnia salt mines contain underground chapels and statues carved from rock salt.

name: Portugal
fact: Lisbon's Belém Tower once helped defend the harbour and commemorates Vasco da Gama's voyage.

name: Qatar
fact: Al Zubarah's ruins preserve a coastal town that grew through pearl diving and trade.

name: Romania
fact: The Danube Delta's lakes and marshes shelter hundreds of bird species before the river reaches the Black Sea.

name: Russia
fact: Siberia's Lake Baikal holds about one fifth of Earth's unfrozen freshwater reserve.

name: Rwanda
fact: Nyungwe National Park protects rainforest habitat for eastern chimpanzees and golden monkeys.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
fact: Brimstone Hill Fortress records the skilled work of enslaved Africans who built this Caribbean stronghold.

name: Saint Lucia
fact: Two steep volcanic peaks, Gros Piton and Petit Piton, rise beside the sea.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
fact: La Soufrière is an active volcano rising above the forested interior of Saint Vincent.

name: Samoa
fact: On Upolu, To Sua is a deep natural swimming hole with a cave connected to the sea.

name: San Marino
fact: A historic town and its fortification towers stand high on Mount Titano.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
fact: These volcanic Gulf of Guinea islands shelter bird species found nowhere else.

name: Saudi Arabia
fact: At Hegra, Nabataean builders carved grand tombs with decorated entrances into rock.

name: Senegal
fact: Gorée Island's historic buildings help people remember enslavement and work toward reconciliation.

name: Serbia
fact: Studenica Monastery has white-marble churches containing centuries-old Byzantine wall paintings.

name: Seychelles
fact: Aldabra's coral islands surround a lagoon and provide a home for giant tortoises.

name: Sierra Leone
fact: The Gola-Tiwai forests shelter pygmy hippopotamuses and white-necked rockfowl.

name: Singapore
fact: A botanic garden founded in 1859 became an important centre for scientific research into rubber cultivation.

name: Slovakia
fact: The Slovak Karst's limestone caves preserve clues to both tropical and icy ancient climates.

name: Slovenia
fact: The Škocjan cave system contains underground passages, waterfalls and enormous limestone chambers.

name: Solomon Islands
fact: On Rennell Island, Lake Tegano was once the lagoon of a coral atoll raised above the sea.

name: Somalia
fact: Laas Geel's rock shelters hold colourful ancient paintings, including cows with decorated necks.

name: South Africa
fact: The Taung skull, discovered in 1924, is a fossil of an early human relative.

name: South Korea
fact: Jeju Island has tunnels left by flowing lava and a volcanic mountain with a crater lake.

name: South Sudan
fact: The White Nile feeds the Sudd, a vast wetland that expands and shrinks with seasonal flooding.

name: Spain
fact: Granada's Alhambra is a hilltop fortress and palace beside the gardens of the Generalife.

name: Sri Lanka
fact: At Sigiriya, stairs lead up Lion's Rock to the ruins of a city on a granite summit.

name: Sudan
fact: Meroe preserves pyramids and temples from the ancient Kingdom of Kush.

name: Suriname
fact: A rainforest reserve protects the upper Coppename River basin and shelters giant river otters.

name: Sweden
fact: Drottningholm's royal palace stands on a lake island beside a theatre built in 1766.

name: Switzerland
fact: The Jungfrau-Aletsch region reveals how glaciers and mountain-building have shaped the Swiss Alps.

name: Syria
fact: Palmyra grew around a desert oasis, where ancient builders blended local, Greek, Roman and Persian influences.

name: Tajikistan
fact: Tajik National Park's Pamir mountains shelter snow leopards among glaciers and hundreds of lakes.

name: Tanzania
fact: The Serengeti's migrating herds include wildebeest, zebras and gazelles searching for water.

name: Thailand
fact: Ayutthaya's surviving towers and monasteries recall its past as a Siamese capital.

name: Timor-Leste
fact: Tais is a handwoven cotton textile whose colours and patterns express Timorese community identities.

name: Togo
fact: In Koutammakou, Batammariba families build distinctive tower-shaped homes from earth.

name: Tonga
fact: Tongatapu's coastline has blowholes where ocean waves send water upward through openings in coral rock.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
fact: At La Brea's Pitch Lake, natural bitumen reaches the surface and cools into asphalt.

name: Tunisia
fact: El Jem has a huge Roman amphitheatre built to hold tens of thousands of spectators.

name: Turkey
fact: At Pamukkale, mineral-rich spring water builds pale terraces and pools along a hillside.

name: Turkmenistan
fact: Ancient Merv was an oasis city on the Silk Road; its ruins span thousands of years.

name: Tuvalu
fact: Nine widely separated, low-lying island and atoll groups make up this Pacific nation.

name: Uganda
fact: Bwindi's forest protects mountain gorillas alongside many kinds of ferns and butterflies.

name: Ukraine
fact: Kyiv's Saint-Sophia Cathedral was designed in the eleventh century to rival Constantinople's Hagia Sophia.

name: United Arab Emirates
fact: Al Ain's ancient settlements include irrigation channels that brought water to desert communities.

name: United Kingdom
fact: Stonehenge and nearby Avebury preserve prehistoric circles of enormous standing stones.

name: United States
fact: Yellowstone has geysers that shoot hot water upward, along with other volcanic heat features.

name: Uruguay
fact: Fray Bentos preserves factories that once prepared and exported meat products across the world.

name: Uzbekistan
fact: Samarkand's historic monuments include Ulugh Beg's observatory, a place for studying the sky.

name: Vanuatu
fact: Chief Roi Mata's Domain connects three islands through archaeology and stories passed down by voice.

name: Venezuela
fact: Canaima National Park contains tepuis: flat-topped mountains with sheer cliffs and waterfalls.

name: Vietnam
fact: Ha Long Bay and Cat Ba have limestone islands rising from the sea like stone towers.

name: Yemen
fact: Socotra's isolated islands shelter many plants, reptiles and land snails found nowhere else.

name: Zambia
fact: At Victoria Falls, the Zambezi plunges into basalt gorges and throws mist high into the air.

name: Zimbabwe
fact: A ruined medieval city preserves the remains of an important Shona trading centre.
